title: An Experimental and Finite Element Protocol to Investigate the Transport of Neutral and Charged Solutes across Articular Cartilage
protocol: Drill out cylindrical osteochondral plugs from cadaveric equine femoral condyles using custom-made drill bit while spraying cool Phosphate-buffered Saline (PBS).
Heat-shrink the osteochondral plugs with a plastic shrinking sleeve.
Mount the osteochondral plug with cartilage at the top initially inside the plastic shrinking sleeve and follow by blowing hot air to it.
Add wet cotton pieces on the surface of cartilage to prevent heat-related damage.
Prepare finite-baths of charged solutes (e.g., 650 µL, 420 mM, ioxaglate).
Prepare finite-baths of neutral solutes (650 µL, 420 mM, iodixanol).
Load the prepared finite-baths on the surface of cartilage using a syringe.
Place a cork plug on the wrapped sample to prevent evaporation during experiments at room temperature.
Place the wrapped samples on a custom-made holder attached to the motorized stage of a micro-CT.
Position the sample so that the cartilage surface covered with contrast agent is facing upward.
Scan the sample using the micro-CT (voxel size of 40 × 40 × 40 µm³, scan time of 2 min, tube voltage of 90 kV and tube current of 180 µA) until equilibrium state (48 h) is reached.
Register 3D images in different time points based on the initial image to facilitate positioning of the Region of Interest using manufacturer's software.
Convert 3D reconstructed micro-CT images into 2D TIFF stack before processing them using manufacturer's software.
Globally segment the cartilage from the subchondral bone and overlying bath in the software.
Obtain the average grey value of cartilage at different time points using the generated cartilage mask.
Use a linear calibration curve to convert average grey values to actual concentration of solutes.
Plot solute concentrations versus experimental time points.
Build finite-bath based cartilage multi-zone models in FEBio.
Assign mechanical and physical properties for different zones of cartilage and bath in FEBio.
Generate mesh with 8-node trilinear hexahedral elements.
Refine the mesh near boundaries.
Apply initial solute concentration in the bath.
Set effective pressure corresponding to the applied solute concentration.
Run the model in transient mode to obtain solute concentration versus time curves based on prescribed diffusion coefficients in different cartilage zones.
Add two monovalent counter-ions to both the bath and the tissue to circumvent electric fluctuation.
Use the same effective fluid pressures and concentrations for steady-state models in cartilage and overlying bath while increasing FCD to its desired value.
Create a well-stirred finite-bath by keeping the solute diffusion coefficient in the bath sufficiently high for transient models.
Inject the solute from the bath-air interface into the bath to reach its desired concentration value.
Remove the prescribed solute concentration boundary condition previously set and revert the diffusion coefficient of the finite-bath to its actual diffusion coefficient.
Run the model again to obtain final solute concentration-time curves based on applied FCDs and diffusion coefficients in different cartilage zones.
Change diffusion coefficients and FCDs in cartilage zones using the FEBio-MATLAB interface.
Run models in FEBio.
Extract solute concentration-time curves from the models.
Compare obtained solute concentration-time curves with experimental data.
Obtain sets of diffusion coefficients and FCDs in different cartilage zones based on minimum root mean square error (RMSE).
